stops.name: Pasterze
stops.detail: With a length of about 8 km, the Pasterze is still the largest glacier in Austria and the longest of the Eastern Alps. It is located at the foot of the Grossglockner in the upper valley floor of the Möll valley (Pasterzenboden) and is the source area of the Möll. Since 1856, their area has decreased by almost half from then over 30 km2. As with the vast majority of Austrian glaciers, their length has been declining for several years, in the last few years on the order of 50 meters per year. In [dated source]/15, the decline was 54.4 m, in [dated source] 52.5 m. By [dated source], the glacier tongue could have disappeared. As of September [dated source], there were forecasts that saw a tearing of the glacier tongue in 1-2 years. At the beginning of [dated source], the forecast was postponed to [dated source] or [dated source]. According to July [dated source], this will happen in the summer of [dated source]. After demolishing the Pasterze, the Gepatschferner in Tyrol is expected to be the largest glacier in Austria.
